title: Naming Binary Molecular Compounds
description: Learn how to name compounds formed between two non-metals.
content:
Binary molecular compounds are formed between two non-metals. Unlike ionic compounds, these compounds use prefixes to indicate the number of atoms of each element in the formula.

The prefixes used are:
- mono- (1) - often omitted for the first element
- di- (2)
- tri- (3)
- tetra- (4)
- penta- (5)
- hexa- (6)
- hepta- (7)
- octa- (8)
- nona- (9)
- deca- (10)

To name a binary molecular compound:
1. Name the first element using its element name
2. Name the second element, changing its ending to '-ide'
3. Add prefixes to both elements to indicate the number of atoms

Examples:
- CO: carbon monoxide (mono- is omitted for the first element)
- CO2: carbon dioxide
- N2O4: dinitrogen tetroxide
- SF6: sulfur hexafluoride

Note: When the prefix ends with 'a' or 'o' and the element name begins with 'o', one of the vowels is often dropped (e.g., 'mono-oxide' becomes 'monoxide').
objectives: Understand the difference between ionic and molecular compounds
Learn the prefixes used to indicate the number of atoms
Write chemical formulas from the names of molecular compounds
